learning_outcomes.description: Apply the principles of Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP) to identify food safety hazards, determine critical control points and develop monitoring and corrective action strategies to ensure the safety and quality of food products.
Use risk analysis approaches to identify, evaluate and manage biological, chemical, physical and allergenic hazards in the food supply chain.
Interpret food regulations, guidelines and codes of practice to evaluate compliance and inform evidence-based decision making in food safety and quality management.
Evaluate foodborne hazards and toxic substances including naturally occurring toxins, contaminants and additives by applying principles of toxicology, exposure assessment and health risk evaluation.

assessments.task_description:
You will complete two invigilated In‑class Online Quizzes designed to help you practise the styles of questions you will encounter in the in‑semester exam and end-of-semester exam.


Quiz 1 will be based on Week 1 lecture content (Introduction to Food Safety).

When: During the scheduled tutorial in Teaching Week 2.

Where: Online via the FOOD3017 Learn.UQ Ultra site accessed on your own electronic device, under invigilation during the Teaching Week 2 Tutorial.

Duration: 20 minutes.

Marks: 20 marks.

Attempts: One attempt only.

Question types: Multiple choice, true/false, short answer and critical thinking/problem-solving.

Weighting: 10% of final course grade.


Quiz 2 will be based on Week 2 lecture content (Food Allergens and Intolerances).

When: During the scheduled tutorial in Teaching Week 4.

Where: Online via the FOOD3017 Learn.UQ Ultra site accessed on your own electronic device, under invigilation during the Teaching Week 4 Tutorial.

Duration: 20 minutes.

Marks: 20 marks.

Attempts: One attempt only.

Question types: Multiple choice, true/false, short answer and critical thinking/problem-solving.

Weighting: 10% of final course grade.


This assessment task evaluates students' abilities, skills and knowledge without the aid of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT). Students are advised that the use of AI or MT technologies to develop responses is strictly prohibited and may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct.

learning_activities.topic:
Lectures

A series of lectures will be delivered to introduce the concepts and importance of food safety, food allergens and quality assurance (QA) in the food industry. HACCP and predictive microbiology-based food safety management tools will be taught, as well as risk analysis. A detailed week-by-week timetable of lecture topics can be accessed in the Blackboard Learning Resources Folder.
